results.name: A1X every write site of quality_remaining is enumerated and matches the expected set (v1 decay = 404/405/409 only; 489 is the v2 path)
RATE the A2 evidence is taken from the PRODUCTION rate function (not a re-derivation): every rate temperature <= hard_upper for its class
SIDE the tightened bound's side conditions are stated AND checked (ambient branch unreachable; ambient > hard_upper for some classes here)

detail.why: ambient branch unreachable: the tightened bound is sound for every present class
detail.note: because ambient (25 C) exceeds the hard upper bound of classes 1 (8 C) and 2 (-12 C), the tightened bound is sound ONLY while those classes stay precooled

results.name: FORCE `_force_return_all` is instrumented: calls and the recorded return-arrival distribution are reported (the truncation is a known optimism, not a silent one)

detail.truncation_note: _force_return_all advances the cold chain only to `depart` (strict_online_env.py:272) while recording the unload at `depart + travel` (:273), so the RECORDED delivered quality is more optimistic than the physics -- which WEAKENS (does not strengthen) the BND check that compares against recorded deliveries

results.name: COV coverage is stated in BOTH directions: bound rows cover N%% of delivered orders, and the unmatched counts are reported explicitly

detail.why_incomplete: the capture covers only the FIRST 14 decision points of the run, so later-revealed orders can never appear in a bound row

results.name: BIND the bound is reported against the thresholds: does it ever classify an order unsalable? (if never, more search cannot help -- the payoff needs a tighter tau_max)

detail.strategic_point: k(T_max)*tau_max is ~0.07/0.06/0.02 for classes 0/1/2 at tau_max=24 h, so the ratios stay far above 0.8/0.85/0.9: the bound currently NEVER binds, and its certification payoff must come from a tighter tau_max (a separate, pre-declared derivation), not from more search

results.name: IQ the not-yet-loaded start quality comes from the DATASET, not a hardcoded 1.0

detail.note: hardcoding 1.0 was correct only because this dataset is 1.0 everywhere; on a dataset with initial_quality < 1 it would silently produce a bound above the true delivered quality
